correctness.rationale: For L=2I-S-S^-1 on ℤ and real α>0, the absolutely summable symmetric coefficients a_k=(-1)^k Γ(2α+1)/(Γ(α-k+1)Γ(α+k+1)) obey a_(k+1)=a_k(k-α)/(k+α+1) and their Fourier sum at zero vanishes. In α between integers m and m+1, recurrence forces sign (-1)^k through k=m+1 and constant tail sign thereafter; hence ℓ1/ℓ∞ convolution norms are exactly the finite positive/negative gamma sums in the finding. At integers m they reduce to 4^m. Evaluating the Fourier multiplier at θ=π and applying Wiener inversion shows spectral radius 4^α on ℓ1 and ℓ∞. Comparing alternating Fourier sum with absolute sum isolates the strictly positive wrong-sign tail for noninteger α; at every positive integer the derivative from zero tail coefficients has jump 4Σ_{j>=0} B(j+1,2m+1)=2/m. Near zero the negative off-origin mass tends to one, giving norm discontinuity and ℓ1 failure, while pointwise small coefficients plus uniform ℓ1 bound imply strong convergence on c0 and interior ℓp; the constant function witnesses ℓ∞ failure. Independently checked sign strips and l1 expressions for α=0.3,1.25,2.6,4.1 with analytically evaluated tails, and cusp beta identity m=1..4. These bounded tests supplement the gamma and Wiener proofs.

value.rationale: A full sharp ℓ1/ℓ∞ operator-norm profile of all fractional powers of the simplest infinite lattice Laplacian is a natural harmonic-analysis invariant. The exact integer-only normaloidity, infinite universal sequence of nonzero first-derivative cusp jumps 2/m, and strong-order-zero endpoint asymmetry locate genuine structural boundaries. The fractional centered-difference coefficients were known; the new contribution is a motivated global operator-norm and topology classification rather than renaming those coefficients.
